question.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}+5\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{x}^{2}+5){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2}+5)({e}^{x})-\int ({e}^{x})(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2}+5){e}^{x}-6\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x={e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x({e}^{x})-\int ({e}^{x})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{e}^{x}-\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{e}^{x}-{e}^{x}+D \\  & ={e}^{x}(x-1)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{x}^{2}+5){e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =(3{x}^{2}+5){e}^{x}-6({e}^{x}(x-1)+D) \\  & =(3{x}^{2}+5){e}^{x}-6{e}^{x}(x-1)+C \\  & ={e}^{x}(3{x}^{2}-6x+11)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$
